method.input: native-cdp-touch, Chromium phone emulation, maximum two contacts
method.graphics: Software-WebGL fallback enabled; renderer not certified
method.inspection_detail: Each captured image was viewed before adapting the next action. Driver acts captured live then paused; map planning remained paused until CLOSE MAP. UI-only discovery; no source, docs, tests, prior reviews, recordings, scripts, hidden state or internal game handles inspected.

anchors.10: Exceptional with no material observed shortcomings

scale.interpretation: Scores describe this one assisted, paused, emulated mobile attempt; no target score used. Limited mission coverage makes gameplay and overall scores provisional.

overall_mobile.reason: Functional portrait touch combat and one successful recovery, but repeated navigation corrections and difficult threat response dominated this short run.

controls.reason: Held FIRE, simultaneous movement/fire and USE/fire worked. Scene swipes turned successfully, but fast rotation needed repeated sweeps, FIRE drag gave only modest correction, and movement around walls was hard to judge.

gameplay.reason: Opening guard, pressure during recovery, regenerating shield and route planning create meaningful decisions. Only the first recovery was reached; later mission balance and variety are unknown.

presentation.reason: Cohesive restrained typography, cyan/amber cues, wet industrial atmosphere and clear recovery/loss panels. Close walls sometimes filled almost the entire world view with little spatial information.

usability.reason: Concise handbook and paused route map supported discovery. Cover navigation and recovering orientation under attack required many corrections; map layout reflowed after Mara became recovered.

readability.reason: Health, ammo, objective and terminal headline are legible at 390 CSS pixels. Small spaced microcopy, compact map detail, threat glyphs and narrow field of view demand attention; terminal stat detail wraps across lines.

controls_exercised: MOVE analog stick: forward, backward, strafe and diagonals
Simultaneous HOLD USE recovery and FIRE drag (two contacts)
Resume via driver visible Resume action
JUMP tap attempted near wall; successful vault not established
DASH tap: cooldown visibly displayed; no phase evade credited

strengths.detail: Opening guard disappeared after sustained fire; initial target is immediately discoverable and supplied a clear onboarding hint. Terminal confirms one elimination.
The paused map shows player orientation, receiver reach rings, obstacles and a walking route; repeatedly useful for diagnosing position.
Recovery changed objective, lit memory slot 01 and displayed a readable named confirmation while retaining combat controls.
Terminal panel clearly distinguishes loss and preserves recovered character plus performance statistics.

friction.detail: Approach overshot the receiver to its north wall. Close wall views removed landmarks; needed map inspection and backward/diagonal correction. This may partly reflect discrete automation holds rather than continuous human thumb feedback.

Repeated attempts to pass the archive corner produced similar wall-filling images while shield depleted and health fell from 100 to 42. Jump did not visibly resolve the obstruction; cannot establish a collision defect from this evidence.

Two long scene swipes were needed to face pursuing enemies. A short FIRE drag barely changed heading, and counterfire/repositioning left only 4 health. Low 4% accuracy reflects my poor aim and shots into walls as well as control friction; not proof of a weapon defect.
Recovered Mara button enlarged and shifted map content down, changing the spatial layout between map visits.

tooling.command_error: Sequence 23 attempted MAP after movement; Selector must be visible. Subsequent capture established actual terminal loss, so this was not a blocker or a second attempt.

missing: AIM, SWAP, CROUCH and RUN behavior

limits: One fresh mission only; no retry.
Native emulation is not physical-device enjoyment or performance validation.
Paused inspection and intermittent touch batches materially alter tempo and planning pressure.
Software WebGL performance cannot stand in for phone GPU performance.
Source identity is user-supplied, not source-inspected.
